solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: War planners try to avoid this church oddball

definitions.text: War planners try to avoid this

parts.note: a mission is a church or chapel set up to serve a district
a creep is an unpleasant, odd sort of person

explanation.surface: Military strategists steer clear of a strange churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole descriptive phrase: the thing generals fear, an operation whose aims keep growing.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the gradual, unplanned widening of a military operation's goals, which commanders dread.

clue.text: Citizen is superior to King raised on island

indicators.note: in a down clue, being superior means sitting higher, so this piece comes first
in a down clue, one piece sitting on another is placed above it
in a down entry, raised means the king's name is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A subject outranks a monarch who was brought up on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LEAR into RAEL in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of the state of Israel is a citizen of that country.

clue.text: Small insect that is circling over drink

indicators.note: circling means these pieces wrap around the next one

parts.note: a moth is an insect
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A little bug flying around above a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts O inside MOTHIE, splitting it after MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A blended fruit drink, often with yoghurt, is a familiar beverage of this name.

clue.text: Boorish lot's heartless boarish noises

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: pigs and boars make oinks

explanation.surface: A rough crowd's grunting, pig-like sounds without any feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes N, the middle letter of OINKS. 'Boorish' and 'boarish' play on the sound alike. An oik is British slang for a crude, uncouth person.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiks is British slang for uncultured, loutish people, a plural fitting a boorish lot.

clue.text: Elaborate lace put on a fruit

indicators.note: to elaborate is to work something out in more detail, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fancy lace is placed upon a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' rearranges LACEPUTONA. It looks like an adjective describing the lace.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet melon with orange flesh, a fruit in the melon family.

clue.text: Lithe juvenile crossing Channel verified

indicators.note: the letters run across the boundary between the two words, so the light is found spanning them

explanation.surface: A supple youngster's Channel swim has been officially confirmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span chann-EL VER-ified. Channel here means the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eel is a slender, sinuous juvenile fish, so lithe juvenile fits.

clue.text: Extremely peevish on stage, setter's full of cold?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of the following word

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
the setter refers to themself, so setter's is my

explanation.surface: An irritable actor on stage, and the crossword compiler has a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' looks theatrical but means a leg of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm is the mucus of a cold, so someone congested and catarrhal is full of it.

clue.text: Prince mixes up crew on main royal vessel

indicators.note: on the main (the open sea) suggests the following piece rides upon this one, placed after it

parts.note: addles means confuses or muddles
a crew is a team
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A prince confuses the sailors aboard a royal ship on the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixes up' looks like an anagram signal but gives ADDLES. 'main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat driven by large paddle wheels is a type of steam-powered vessel.

clue.text: Nobleman entombed in rotten clay slab reportedly

indicators.note: a body entombed is enclosed, so the noble goes inside the other letters
something rotten has broken down, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat buried under a crumbling clay slab, or so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' makes BYALLACS, and 'entombed in' places the nobleman inside it; 'reportedly' looks like a homophone signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means according to what people say, just as reportedly does.

clue.text: Leaderless congregation on song in chamber

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

indicators.note: leaderless means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a flock is a congregation, the faithful led by a pastor

explanation.surface: A church choir without its leader is singing in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' takes F from FLOCK, leaving LOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed compartment between two areas of differing pressure is a type of chamber.

clue.text: Trinket from Ely on TV broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A knick-knack from the cathedral city of Ely features on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges ELYONTV. Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap small ornament or toy is a trinket, often sold as a gimmick.

clue.text: Dutch world German inhabited

parts.note: Welt is the German word for world

explanation.surface: A Dutch, global and German community lived there.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a list of nationalities; 'German' says to translate 'world'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lived somewhere is to have resided there, so the past tense fits.

clue.text: Girl east of capital briefly gets work

indicators.note: in an across clue, east of means placed to the right, after
briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Madrid is the Spanish capital
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman from beyond the city finds a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts MADRID to MADRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A part song for several voices is a musical work or composition.

clue.text: State of dirty items not being spun

parts.note: the washing is a pile of dirty clothes to be laundered

indicators.note: being spun means turned round, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A condition where the dirty laundry is not going round in the machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being spun' reverses NOT to TON; the laundry surface makes spinning look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Pacific Northwest bears this name.

clue.text: Assassin maybe destroyed lair on time

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A hit man wrecked a hideout right on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges LAIRONTIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer removes people, so an assassin is one example of someone who eliminates.

clue.text: Flyer mailed, initially a single one returned

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word
returned means sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: any can mean a single one, as in pick any

explanation.surface: A leaflet was posted, but at first one copy came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses ANY to YNA. 'Flyer' looks like a leaflet but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This Asian starling, a talking bird, is a creature that flies.

clue.text: Shell various planes blockading empty hangar

indicators.note: blockading means surrounding and closing in, so these letters enclose the others
various suggests differently arranged, so these letters are reordered
empty means the inside of the word is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Assorted aircraft blocking an unused hangar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' gives SAPNEL; 'empty' keeps only the outside letters of hangar, and 'blockading' means the jumbled planes surround them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragments of an exploded shell, or the shell itself, are called by this name.

clue.text: Check what your cardiologist wants to hear

definitions.meaning: a mark made to show something is correct or checked

definitions.text: what your cardiologist wants to hear
definitions.meaning: the regular beat of a healthy heart

explanation.surface: A heart doctor checks for a healthy beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A check mark and a steady heartbeat are both called by this name.

clue.text: Beverage doubly acceptable in castle

parts.note: cha and tea are both names for the same drink, so it is given twice
U stands for upper-class, hence acceptable

explanation.surface: Twice the drink is fine in a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is slang for tea, so the drink appears in two forms. U is the British label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A French castle or large country house is known by this name.

clue.text: One who's been down the aisle too often

definitions.text: One who's been down the aisle too often

parts.words: One who's been down the aisle too often
parts.note: the aisle suggests a wedding, but here it is a supermarket aisle visited compulsively

explanation.surface: A serial bride or groom who keeps marrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down the aisle' suggests weddings; the aisle is in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A compulsive buyer keeps wandering store aisles, a person addicted to purchasing.

clue.text: Rest of fleet is regularly taken out, of course

indicators.note: regularly taken out means every other letter is removed, leaving the alternate letters

parts.note: sure is said for of course, certainly

explanation.surface: Part of the fleet is withdrawn at intervals, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing alternate letters F, E, T, S of 'fleet is' leaves LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time away from work is rest or relaxation.

clue.text: Mains gas supply coming together

indicators.note: read as supple-y, supply means flexibly, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: The provision of piped mains gas is being connected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' rearranges MAINSGAS; read as an adverb it means in a supple way.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathering into a mass or crowd means assembling, coming together.

clue.text: Endure mostly being interrupted by old Greek

indicators.note: being interrupted means having something break in, so a letter goes inside
mostly means nearly all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: to stick something is to endure or tolerate it

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek mostly puts up with being cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts STICK to STIC; O goes inside. 'Greek' is a definition: Stoic philosophy came from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Zeno's school of philosophy in ancient Athens was a Greek thinker.

clue.text: See you with something rolled in gold

indicators.note: in means this piece goes inside the next one

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is rolled in games

explanation.surface: Farewell, wrapped in a golden cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something rolled' is a die, the dice cube.
explanation.definitionFit: A French farewell, used in English to say goodbye, like see you.

clue.text: Governor finally spoke on Russian station

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
finally points to the closing letter of the next word

parts.note: Mir was the Russian space station

explanation.surface: The administrator eventually spoke on a Russian radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' suggests radio; Mir was the space station.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim ruler or commander, especially in the Middle East, governs a territory.

clue.text: Remove bumps from transport to venue

indicators.note: to transport is to carry away or move, so these letters are moved into new positions

explanation.surface: Smoothing the road from the bus to the venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' rearranges TOVENUE; it looks like a noun for buses.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a surface flat or level is to get rid of its bumps.

clue.text: Number caged in staff shelter: a tiger's revenge?

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it

indicators.note: caged in means held within, so this letter goes inside the next piece

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: A captive animal in a zoo shelter dreams of getting its own back.
explanation.walkthrough: Usually people hunt tigers; the question mark flags the tables turned, a tiger chasing a human.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised search for a person; a tiger stalking humans would be the reverse of a tiger hunt.

clue.text: Strange Scottish books turn editor wild

parts.note: unco is the Scots word for strange or unusual
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: Odd Scottish volumes make an editor go mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like an anagram signal but is defined by the Scots UNCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrestrained and out of control is wild.
